summary: Blog seed-form exposes only blacklist scope — no whitelist/'limit-to' mode, so generation can't be restricted to a chosen set of traditions
description:
User report: the tradition filter in the blog section 'doesn't work for limiting the scope of the blog posts.'

ROOT CAUSE — UI gap, not a backend bug. The seed-form only offers a blacklist ("Scope — block traditions"); checked boxes always mean EXCLUDE. There is no whitelist/'limit-to' control, so a post cannot be restricted to only a chosen set of traditions (you'd have to block the other ~14). Confirmed empirically: across all blog_posts, 1 seed ever used blacklist (honored correctly, zero violations) and 0 seeds ever used whitelist.

The backend already fully supports whitelist end-to-end:
- src/app/api/admin/blog/seed/route.ts:17 SCOPE_MODES includes 'whitelist'; :77 reads whitelisted_traditions
- src/lib/admin-blog.ts insertSeed persists whitelisted_traditions
- src/lib/blog-generate.ts:241-255 seedToPrefs maps 'whitelist' through to UserPreferences
- src/lib/graph.ts:341-351 buildScopeFilter emits tradition = ANY($n) for whitelist; applied by all 3 retrieval legs (vector/graph/lexical)

FIX (UI-only, no backend changes): add a scope-mode toggle to seed-form.tsx (src/app/(admin)/admin/blog/seed-form.tsx:59-83,221-233) so the checked traditions can mean either Block (current blacklist) or Limit-to (whitelist -> POST scope_mode:'whitelist' + whitelisted_traditions:[...]).

TEST: a unit/integration test asserting the form POSTs scope_mode:'whitelist' with whitelisted_traditions when the limit-to mode is selected (the seed route already validates it).
